text:
arjun: Quick sketch — proposal for a graceful-degrade "fanout" lane on dedicated GPU pools when capacity is tight. Goal: let more tenants stay up with lower throughput (and bounded quality cost) instead of wholesale preemptions. want thoughts on operator vs control-plane responsibilities.

mica: interesting. do you mean throttling per-tenant concurrency or sampling/shorter generations?

arjun: both. main idea: introduce a runtime degradation mode that has two levers — concurrency cap (soft) and generation budget (tokens per request). when in degrade mode we 1) reduce per-tenant concurrency, 2) force a sampling policy for large-gen requests (e.g., max_tokens override), 3) optionally route low-priority traffic to smaller quantized variants.

sam: how would we surface this in the allocator/operator API? operator shouldn't need to understand tenant semantics.

arjun: thinking: control-plane marks a pool as CONSTRAINED and sets a DegradeProfile. operator implements enforcement primitives (concurrency limiter, token-injector) per-tenant. contract: DegradeProfile is small and dumb — only numbers and policy flags. operator reports enforcement metrics.

dina: can you paste a tiny example profile?

arjun: sure:
```yaml
degrade_profile: 
  name: fanout-compact-v1
  concurrency_factor: 0.5        # multiply tenant concurrency limits by this
  max_tokens_per_req: 256       # force short responses in degrade mode
  prefer_quantized_variant: true
  fallback_delay_ms: 150        # allow brief tail to try full model once before enforcing
  p99_tail_latency_budget_ms: 300
```

mica: i like the concision. fallback_delay is neat as an escape hatch — try to finish existing inflight heavy requests.

sam: what about safety/quality regressions? we need a way to measure user-visible regressions and auto-unwind the degrade.

arjun: telemetry-bot will report quality-regression signals to the control-plane: token_truncation_rate, avg_response_length_change, rerank_loss_rate. policy includes thresholds to auto-escalate (un-degrade) or broaden degradation.

telemetry-bot: ping — sample metrics that will matter: p50_latency, p95_latency, queue_length, token_drop_rate, quantized_fallback_rate, tenant_error_rate.

dina: operator-side: are we comfortable with per-tenant enforcement? that means operator needs tenant identifiers in admission path. previously operator was tenant-agnostic for fairness.

arjun: agreed. tradeoff: to fanout, operator must see tenant id for limiting. we keep billing/charge separation by only passing opaque tenant_id; no PII. operator enforces but control-plane owns policy.

sam: edge case: bursts from a single tenant could hijack the fanout lane — do we have a global cap?

arjun: yes — DegradeProfile includes global_shares and tenant_max_share. admission path will first apply global pool-level caps, then tenant-level. example: max_tenants=20, tenant_max_share=0.1.

mica: rollout plan? i propose phases: 1) metrics-only (operator sim enforcement, report what would be rate-limited), 2) soft-enforce (reject with 429 + header X-Degrade-Mode), 3) hard-enforce with quantized routing.

arjun: +1. also want a canary on low-traffic tenants first. add feature flag for each pool.

dina: observability checklist: show per-tenant p99, token truncation, fallback_count, enforcement_actions. add logs for 'degrade-triggered' with reason code (capacity|taillatency|slo-breach).

ops-bot: deploy request queued: staging/operator-degrade-mode v1 -> canary. triggered by @dina.

sam: one more: API boundary question — should DegradeProfile live in the same API group as capacity/scale policy or in routing config? mixing it with scaling makes sense because both are capacity signals. but routing teams may feel it's collide.

arjun: i'd prefer scale-policy group with a degrade subsection. it keeps all capacity controls in one place. we can add a routing hint field for prefer_quantized_variant so routing can react.

mica: security note — if operator gets tenant ids, ensure RBAC prevents leaks in logs. redact in any operator debug dumps.

arjun: agreed. will add `operator_log_redaction: true` default.

dina: sounds practical. can we set thresholds for auto-rollback? e.g., if tenant_error_rate > 1% after enforce, unwind.

arjun: yes — add unwind thresholds: error_rate_pct, quality_delta_pct, sustained_duration_s.

sam: ok next steps: write a short RFC addendum with API sketch (DegradeProfile proto), rollout phases, telemetry contract, and operator implementation checklist. I'll take proto sketch. @mica will own telemetry contract. @dina will own rollout + canary.

arjun: thanks. I'll drop the first draft in docs/rfcs and tag the RFC PR here.

mica: :thumbsup:

arjun: closing with a note — this aims to prefer graceful QoS shaping over preemptions; still want fail-states (hard preempt) when safety requires it.

telemetry-bot: noted. creating dashboard draft `degrade-mode/summary` and feed for alerting.

ops-bot: canary deploy scheduled at 2025-09-12T22:00Z.
